texts: The stones that pave the Cliff Path are flat and sea-worn.

good. the definite plural becomes a stone group, the restrictive relative is kept as a real paving event with the path as its object, and both predicates (flat, sea-worn) reach each individual stone through fireable per-member rules. "Cliff Path" gets one name symbol plus its kind atom, so nothing is lost.
The bones of the old graveyard lie under the water in the Sunken Cove.

good. the postural "lie" is recorded as a position rather than an invented event, "under" keeps its own surface preposition instead of being flattened into containment, and "in the Sunken Cove" is carried on the water it modifies. The bones' position attaches to each bone through a fireable rule rather than to the group as a whole, which is the only soft spot and costs no content, so no rewrite is needed.
The Sunken Cove holds a single lantern.
The iron bands reinforce the Stilllight Lantern.

bad: "a single lantern" packs an exact count into a singular indefinite, and the translator has no count carrier there, so it slotted "single" as a description of the lantern - asserting the lantern is single rather than that the cove holds exactly one. Rewrite as "The Sunken Cove holds only one lantern.", which puts the count where the translator's exact-count machinery can take it (a lantern group counted at one) instead of in a property slot. The extra exclusive shade of "single"/"only" is a known unrepresented gap and will not be recorded either way, but the count itself then survives.

good. the definite plural becomes an iron_band group carrying the compound's genus (band), the named lantern gets one opaque symbol with its Name and kind atoms, and the reinforcing reaches each band through a fireable per-member rule while the group-level event stays queryable.
good. the Council stays one definite body, the tide-pools become a group of tide-pools, and the surveying event carries both participants with nothing dropped.
The lanterns at the Hollows stand along the forest paths.
The lanterns at the Hollows burn dimly.
good. the standing is recorded as a position rather than an invented happening: the lantern group sits at the Hollows and runs along the forest paths, and every piece of the sentence is carried.

mixed: the location, the lantern group, the dimness and the per-lantern distribution are all right, but the parse records the lanterns as the deliberate doer of the burning instead of as the things that are burning, which overstates them as volitional actors and would make these records miss a query written the other way. If you want wording the translator cannot mis-slot, say "The lanterns at the Hollows are lit, and their light is dim." — the lit state and the dimness then each land in a fixed slot with no subject-role choice to make.
A market runs in the village square every week.
Every distillation requires sea-water from the Salt-bloom Tide-pools.
good. the market stays one specific market rather than markets in general, the village square is carried as where it runs, and "every week" is recorded as a weekly recurrence.

good. the rule is fireable for any distillation and carries the sea-water together with its Salt-bloom Tide-pools origin; the one loose end — how we type a plural place name whose last word is also a kind word — is an open question on our side that no rewording of your sentence would settle.
Whenever the moon is full, Hesper reports essence production to the Council.

(: whenever_rule (Implication (And (Member $x full) (Experiencer $x sk_moon_1)) (And (Member (sk_report $x) report) (Agent (sk_report $x) hesper) (Theme (sk_report $x) essence_production) (Recipient (sk_report $x) sk_council_1) (During (sk_report $x) $x))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

mixed: the content is all there (Hesper as reporter, essence production as what is reported, the Council as addressee, one report per full moon), but the trigger clause is a bare state — "the moon is full" — so the rule waits for a reified full-moon state rather than an event, and a later plain sentence such as "The moon is full." produces only the flat form and would never fire it. Give the trigger a verb so each full moon is an occurrence the rule can bind: "Whenever the moon becomes full, Hesper reports essence production to the Council."
Tessa Brae walks the base of the cliff each morning during the molting season.

good. the habitual walk comes out complete: Tessa Brae as the walker, the base linked to the cliff as its part, "each morning" as a morning slot with a daily cycle, and the molting season as the interval the walking sits inside.
Marra Tallowhand keeps a detailed log every night.
Council members often consult Marra Tallowhand's logs.
good. the nightly habit is fully covered — Marra Tallowhand as keeper, the log with its "detailed" property, and "every night" as a night slot plus a daily cycle.

good. it becomes a fireable rule that hands each council member their own consulting event over Marra Tallowhand's logs, with "often" carried both as the rule's strength and as a recorded quantifier word.
When a week is a high-wraith week, two Keepers tend the Stilllight Lantern together.

good. the high-wraith-week condition, the pair of Keepers as a counted group, the collective "together" reading and the named Stilllight Lantern all land in one fireable per-week rule, with nothing dropped.
good. the "every Keeper's coat" universal becomes a fireable rule that gives each Keeper his own coat, and the mire-essence, the staining and the coat-to-Keeper link are all carried.
A few Keepers each keep a notebook that lists moth-counts and weather notes.

(: keepers_rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_group_1) (And (Member (sk_keep $x) keep) (Agent (sk_keep $x) $x) (Theme (sk_keep $x) (sk_notebook $x)) (Member (sk_notebook $x) notebook) (Member (sk_list $x) list) (Agent (sk_list $x) (sk_notebook $x)) (Theme (sk_list $x) moth_count) (Theme (sk_list $x) weather_note))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

mixed: the group of Keepers, the "a few" count and each Keeper's own notebook all come through, but the notebook's two contents were packed into a single listing record holding both objects at once instead of one record per content, which is not the shape the translator is supposed to produce for a coordinated object. Repeat the verb so each content gets its own clause: "A few Keepers each keep a notebook that lists moth-counts and that lists weather notes." Separately, a capitalised plural label under a count ("A few Keepers") sits on a boundary our instruction set has not yet settled; writing it lowercase, "a few keepers", removes any risk of it being read as a proper name instead of as members of the keeper class.
Whenever the moon is full, the Council meets.

good. parses as a fireable recurrence rule: the full-moon condition becomes the rule's trigger (a state of the moon), and every occurrence of it mints its own Council meeting tied to that same occasion, so the recurrence, the condition and both participants are all carried. "The Council" is correctly read as one collective body rather than a proper name or a set of members.

good. the deciding is recorded as a standing habit of the Council rather than a one-off past act, the Council stays a single collective actor (no per-member claims invented), and "by consensus" is kept as the means by which the deciding is done, so nothing in the sentence is dropped.
Whenever the moon is full, the Council redistributes mire-essence reserves.

(: whenever_full_redistribute (Implication (And (Member $x full) (Experiencer $x sk_moon_1)) (And (Member (sk_redistribute $x) redistribute) (Agent (sk_redistribute $x) sk_council_1) (Theme (sk_redistribute $x) mire_essence_reserve) (During (sk_redistribute $x) $x))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

good. same fireable recurrence shape as the meeting sentence: the full-moon condition triggers a redistribution per occasion, with the Council as the actor and the reserves as what is redistributed. "mire-essence reserves" is kept whole as its own kind and also linked to "reserve", so a later question about reserves in general still reaches it.
Whenever a Keeper retires, the Council staffs that Keeper's station again.
Whenever a Keeper dies, the Council staffs that Keeper's station again.
Letters from neighbouring villages are read aloud by the Council.

(: keeper_retire_staff (Implication (And (Member $e retire) (Agent $e $k) (Member $k keeper)) (And (Member (sk_staff $e) staff) (Agent (sk_staff $e) sk_council_1) (Patient (sk_staff $e) (sk_station $k)) (Member (sk_station $k) station) (Possession (sk_station $k) $k) (During (sk_staff $e) $e) (Again (sk_staff $e)))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

(: keeper_die_staff_rule (Implication (And (Member $k keeper) (Member $e die) (Patient $e $k)) (And (Member (sk_staff $e) staff) (Agent (sk_staff $e) sk_council_1) (Theme (sk_staff $e) (sk_station $k)) (Member (sk_station $k) station) (Possession (sk_station $k) $k) (Again (sk_staff $e)) (During (sk_staff $e) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

(: letters_read_rule (Implication (And (Member $x letter) (From $x $v) (Member $v village) (Member $v neighbouring)) (And (Member (sk_read $x) read) (Agent (sk_read $x) sk_council_1) (Theme (sk_read $x) $x) (Manner (sk_read $x) aloud))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

good. the whenever-condition becomes a fireable rule that triggers on any Keeper's retirement, and the response carries everything the sentence states: the Council as the one staffing, that same Keeper's station as what gets staffed, the timing link back to the retirement, and the "again".

good. same fireable whenever-shape as the retirement sentence: a Keeper's death binds the trigger, and the Council's re-staffing of that Keeper's station, the timing link and the "again" all come through intact.

good. the bare-plural subject and its "from neighbouring villages" restriction both ride into the rule's condition, so the reading fires per letter, with the Council as the reader and "aloud" recorded as the manner — nothing lost.
The Council rarely orders Keepers to burn wintergloss.
(: order_bundle (And (Member sk_order_1 order) (Agent sk_order_1 sk_council_1) (Theme sk_order_1 sk_burn_1)) (STV 0.1 0.9))

good. adjudicated accept — "rarely" is carried on both channels (a low truth-strength on the ordering plus an explicit "rarely" record), and "orders Keepers to burn wintergloss" is routed as object control, with the Keepers as the burners and wintergloss as what is burned. One thing to be aware of rather than to rewrite: the solid spelling "wintergloss" is read as modifier + head, so the parse also asserts that a wintergloss is a kind of gloss — harmless if that holds in the lore, mildly wrong if the plant name is arbitrary.
Twenty-six years ago, a lone wraith emerged.

good. the whole sentence lands — the wraith, its being lone kept as a separate description rather than fused into the kind, the emerging with the wraith as the one who emerged, past tense, and the twenty-six-year gap measured back from now.
Replacement lanterns do not need a touch from the Council.
good. the denial parses as a fireable rule over replacement lanterns, with the Council typed at top level and the "a touch" witness kept inside the denial, so no content is lost or over-asserted.
Tessa Brae walks every part of the base of the cliff each morning during the molting season.
The collectors record the collection in a Watch ledger each morning.

(: walk_rule (Implication (PartOf $y sk_base_1) (And (Member (sk_walk $y) walk) (Agent (sk_walk $y) tessa_brae) (Theme (sk_walk $y) $y) (Time (sk_walk $y) morning) (Every (sk_walk $y) 1 day) (During (sk_walk $y) sk_molting_season_1))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

(: lo27_rule (Implication (PartOf $x sk_group_1) (And (Member (sk_record $x) record) (Agent (sk_record $x) $x) (Theme (sk_record $x) sk_collection_1) (Location (sk_record $x) sk_ledger_1) (Time (sk_record $x) morning) (Every (sk_record $x) 1 day))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

good. "every part of" routes into a per-part rule that carries the walker, the part walked, the each-morning schedule and the molting-season window together, and it fires as soon as any part of the base is named.

good. the daily recording parses both as one group event and as a per-collector rule, with the collection, the Watch ledger and the every-morning schedule all covered; the only open point is an internal head choice (whether a written medium counts as a location), which costs no content.
In distillation, salt is not a substitute for sea-water.
The sea-water store draws from the deep ebb at the mouth of the harbor.
(: salt_sub_distill (In (And (Inheritance salt substitute) (For substitute sea_water)) distillation) (STV 0.0 0.9))

bad: "is not a substitute for X" has no shape the translator can build — the "for sea-water" complement ends up hanging off the bare word "substitute" rather than off salt, and the whole claim (the "in distillation" restriction included) gets buried inside a preposition atom, so nothing about salt is queryable and "sea-water" loses its link to water. Say it with a plain verb and a modal instead, which has a licensed kind-level form and a licensed slot for the domain restriction: "In distillation, salt cannot replace sea-water."
good. the store, the drawing, the deep ebb it draws from and the ebb's position at the mouth are all covered, with the mouth linked to the harbor as a part.
Whenever a Keeper marries a member of a fisher family, that Keeper keeps the station.

(: keeper_marry_rule (Implication (And (Member $k keeper) (Member $e marry) (Agent $e $k) (Theme $e $m) (Member $f fisher_family) (PartOf $m $f)) (And (Member (sk_keep $e) keep) (Agent (sk_keep $e) $k) (Theme (sk_keep $e) sk_station_1) (During (sk_keep $e) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

good. the "whenever" condition becomes a fireable rule that mints one keeping per marriage occasion, with "that Keeper" correctly tied back to the same Keeper who married and the definite station typed at top level; every participant of the sentence is covered.
Keepers carry a notched candle for time-keeping.

(: lo31_rule (Implication (Member $x keeper) (And (Member (sk_carry $x) carry) (Agent (sk_carry $x) $x) (Theme (sk_carry $x) (sk_candle $x)) (Member (sk_candle $x) candle) (Member (sk_candle $x) notched) (For (sk_candle $x) sk_keep_1))) (STV 0.9 0.9))

mixed: the generic rule itself is fine and fireable (every Keeper carries their own notched candle), but the purpose phrase "for time-keeping" is a bare noun-phrase adjunct the translator has no settled slot for: it ended up hung on the candle rather than on the carrying, and the time-keeping itself became a single shared eventuality instead of one per Keeper, so "why do Keepers carry a candle?" does not resolve cleanly. State the purpose as a plain infinitive clause on the verb instead: "Keepers carry a notched candle to keep time."
Wraiths rise from the water in the Sunken Cove.
Every Keeper believes that the people who died in the storm-surge became wraiths.

(: keeper_believe_rule (Implication (Member $k keeper) (And (Member (sk_believe $k) believe) (Experiencer (sk_believe $k) $k) (Theme (sk_believe $k) (And (Member sk_die_1 die) (Patient sk_die_1 sk_people_1) (Location sk_die_1 sk_storm_surge_1) (Past sk_die_1) (Implication (PartOf $y sk_people_1) (And (Member (sk_die $y) die) (Patient (sk_die $y) $y) (Location (sk_die $y) sk_storm_surge_1) (Past (sk_die $y)))) (Member sk_become_1 become) (Patient sk_become_1 sk_people_1) (Past sk_become_1) (Member sk_wraith_1 wraith) (Experiencer sk_wraith_1 sk_people_1) (Result sk_become_1 sk_wraith_1) (Implication (PartOf $z sk_people_1) (Member $z wraith)))))) (STV 1.0 0.9))
good. parses as a fireable generic rule giving each wraith its own rising out of the water, with the Sunken Cove kept as one named place carrying its kind.

good. the "every Keeper" universal becomes a fireable rule, and the belief content is sealed so nothing about the drowned people is asserted as fact — which is what the sentence says. The one point the blind reviewer raised was overturned on adjudication, so no rewrite is needed.

good. the bare plural gives a fireable per-keeper rule, the definite "the wraith rule" is typed at top level (with its compound genus) so it can be referred to elsewhere, and the knowing is recorded as a stative Experiencer/Stimulus pair with nothing invented or lost.
No wraith has emerged in twenty-six years.

mixed: the denial, the per-wraith rule and the explicit "no" all come through and the rule fires, but the twenty-six-year window rests on the translator reading a bare "in twenty-six years" as "within the last twenty-six years" — a reading the instruction set licenses only for an explicit backward-window phrase, so a later re-parse could drop the window or slot it as a duration instead. Make the window explicit: "No wraith has emerged in the past twenty-six years."
Four wraiths rose sixty-three years ago.

good. the count rides a group witness, the rising is recorded both for the group and as a fireable per-member rule (so a wraith named later inherits it), and "sixty-three years ago" anchors on now as a measured gap — all four wraiths and the timing are covered.
The keepers cannot count the sky-cats exactly.
(: cannot_count (And (Member sk_count_1 count) (Agent sk_count_1 sk_group_1) (Theme sk_count_1 sk_group_2) (Can sk_count_1) (Manner sk_count_1 exactly)) (STV 0.0 0.99))

bad: "cannot ... exactly" makes the negation swallow the whole counting event, so the parse says the keepers cannot count the sky-cats at all; the point of the sentence (they can count them, just not precisely) is lost, and the inability is recorded only of the keepers as a body rather than of each keeper. Split the two claims into plain finite clauses, one thing each: "The keepers can count the sky-cats, but they cannot give an exact number."
good. the bare-plural habit becomes a fireable rule that gives each keeper their own using event, and "the crowd rule" is typed and linked to the general kind rule.
Whenever a sky-cat hunts on the Cliff Path, the lanterns at the Hollows gain nightmoths.
The displaced nightmoths keep the lanterns at the Hollows productive.

(: lo39_rule (Implication (And (Member $x hunt) (Agent $x $y) (Member $y sky_cat) (Location $x cliff_path)) (And (Member (sk_gain $x) gain) (Agent (sk_gain $x) sk_lantern_1) (Theme (sk_gain $x) night_moth) (During (sk_gain $x) $x))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

good. the whenever-condition becomes a fireable rule: any sky-cat hunting on the Cliff Path triggers a gain of nightmoths at the Hollows lanterns, tied to that hunt in time, with both places and both creatures typed. One note on our side rather than your wording: "nightmoths" came out here as night_moth but as nightmoth in the next sentence, so the two sentences' moths do not yet share one symbol.

mixed: the group-level reading is right (the displaced moths keep the Hollows lanterns productive, with the productive state and its continuation recorded), but the parse also adds a rule saying each individual nightmoth keeps those lanterns, which the sentence does not claim - the effect is the swarm's jointly - and that per-moth version drops the "productive" result, so it degenerates into each moth merely holding the lanterns. Mark the joint effect so the claim stays at the group level: "Together, the displaced nightmoths keep the lanterns at the Hollows productive."
Tessa Brae's collectors gather the fallen feathers each morning during the molting season.
Ground feathers of sky-cats ward lanterns against wraiths.

(: ward_rule (Implication (And (Member $f ground_feather) (Member $c sky_cat) (PartOf $f $c)) (And (Member (sk_ward $f $c) ward) (Agent (sk_ward $f $c) $f) (Theme (sk_ward $f $c) lantern) (Against (sk_ward $f $c) wraith))) (STV 0.9 0.9))
good. the bare plural becomes a fireable per-sky-cat rule, the molting sky-cat is recorded as the one undergoing the molt, and "late summer" rides the event's time slot.

mixed: nothing is lost and the rule fires, but this time the molting sky-cat is recorded as a volitional doer rather than as the one undergoing the molt — and the otherwise identical "late summer" sentence above got it right, so this is a translator slip rather than anything wrong with your wording. No rewrite would fix it reliably; keep the sentence as written and have it re-parsed.

mixed: the group-level event covers everything — the gathering, the morning slot, the daily cycle and the molting-season window — but the extra per-collector rule the parser adds carries none of the three time restrictions, so it claims each collector gathers the fallen feathers at any hour of any season. Making the subject a single collective body removes that split entirely: "Tessa Brae's collecting crew gathers the fallen feathers each morning during the molting season." If you need each collector to stay individually queryable, keep your plural wording and have it re-parsed instead — the fault is in the rule the translator built, not in your sentence.

good. the of-phrase ties the feathers to sky-cats, the ground-feather restriction rides in the rule's premise, and both the lanterns warded and the wraiths warded against are covered. Two things worth knowing: "ground" is recorded as a property of the feathers, so "ground up" and "lying on the ground" are not distinguished, and the rule only fires for feathers still registered as belonging to a sky-cat — which the gathered feathers of the previous sentence are not.
Wraiths that are in the cove sometimes harm sky-cats.
When a moth-count at the Stilllight Lantern is low, sky-cats stay on the cliff-spires.
(: skycat_rule (Implication (And (Member $x sky_cat) (Member $c moth_count) (LocatedIn $c stilllight_lantern) (Member $c low)) (On $x sk_spires_1)) (STV 1.0 0.9))

good. the relative clause becomes the rule's condition (a wraith that is in the cove), "sometimes" both sets the rule's strength and is kept as the quantifier word, and the cove itself is asserted so the rule can actually fire.

mixed: the rule fires and the condition — a low moth-count at the Stilllight Lantern — is fully captured, but "stay on" collapses into a bare position statement, so the output cannot tell "stay on the cliff-spires" from "are on the cliff-spires" and the remaining/continuing sense is lost. If that sense matters, hang the continuation on a predicate rather than on the preposition: "When a moth-count at the Stilllight Lantern is low, sky-cats remain perched on the cliff-spires." — the translator has a carrier for continuation on a predicate, but none on a bare locative.
Tide-pools are dry at neap tide.

mixed: the important part is right — dryness is tied to the neap-tide condition and is not asserted of tide-pools in general — but the parser also emits a taxonomy atom classifying a neap tide as "neap", which says slightly more than your sentence does. That is a translator slip rather than a wording problem: the sentence is already in the ideal shape for a conditional property, so leave it as written and have it re-parsed.

mixed: the claim itself lands correctly as a kind-level "salt-bloom needs spring-tide fills", but the parser adds an unstated taxonomy atom about spring tides, and once that atom is dropped the stacked compound "spring-tide fills" is one opaque label with nothing tying it back to spring tides — a later question about spring tides will not reach this rule. Un-stack the modifier so each piece keeps its own symbol: "Salt-bloom needs spring tides to fill the tide-pools." (that names the tide-pools as what gets filled — substitute whatever your lore has the spring tide fill).
The keepers cannot explain the moon-phase rule.
(: lo49_neg (And (Member sk_explain_1 explain) (Agent sk_explain_1 sk_group_1) (Theme sk_explain_1 sk_rule_1) (Can sk_explain_1)) (STV 0.0 0.99))

good. the denial is recorded twice as it should be — the keepers as a body cannot explain it, and no individual keeper can either — and both forms are usable by the reasoner, with the keepers, the rule itself and its genus 'rule' all kept outside the denial so they stay true.
Whenever a spring tide ends, a Cauldron Hall apprentice refills the cisterns from the deep ebb.

(: whenever_tide_refill (Implication (And (Member $t spring_tide) (Member $x end) (Patient $x $t)) (And (Member (sk_refill $x) refill) (Agent (sk_refill $x) (sk_apprentice $x)) (Member (sk_apprentice $x) apprentice) (Possession (sk_apprentice $x) cauldron_hall) (Patient (sk_refill $x) sk_cistern_1) (Source (sk_refill $x) sk_ebb_1) (During (sk_refill $x) $x))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

good. the whenever-rule is fireable: the ending of a spring tide is the trigger, and each occurrence mints its own Cauldron Hall apprentice performing the refilling, with the cisterns, the deep ebb as source, and the time-link back to the tide all covered.
Whenever a winter night is clear, the cold-threshold wind comes off the Cold Sea.
Whenever a Keeper mixes salt-bloom into mire-essence, that mire-essence burns slowly.
Whenever a cold-threshold night comes, unprepared lanterns on the Cliff Path die.

(: whenever_clear_wind (Implication (And (Member $n winter_night) (Member $n clear)) (And (Member (sk_come $n) come) (Patient (sk_come $n) sk_wind_1) (Source (sk_come $n) cold_sea) (During (sk_come $n) $n))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

(: whenever_mix_burn (Implication (And (Member $k keeper) (Member $e mix) (Agent $e $k) (Theme $e salt_bloom) (Goal $e $m) (Member $m mire_essence)) (And (Member (sk_burn $e) burn) (Patient (sk_burn $e) $m) (Manner (sk_burn $e) slowly) (During (sk_burn $e) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

(: night_lantern_die_rule (Implication (And (Member $e come) (Theme $e $n) (Member $n cold_threshold_night) (Member $l lantern) (Member $l unprepared) (On $l cliff_path)) (And (Member (sk_die $e $l) die) (Patient (sk_die $e $l) $l) (During (sk_die $e $l) $e))) (STV 1.0 0.9))

mixed: everything is captured and the rule fires, but the trigger is a state ("a winter night IS clear") rather than a happening, so there is no occurrence for the consequence to be timed against and the wind's coming ends up hung on the night itself — a corner the instruction set does not settle. Make the trigger an event, as your third sentence already does: "Whenever a clear winter night falls, the cold-threshold wind comes off the Cold Sea."

mixed: the rule fires and says the right thing, but "that mire-essence" points back at a bare substance word, which is normally treated as the stuff in general and not as a particular quantity, so there is nothing licensed for the demonstrative to pick out; the parse individuates the mire-essence anyway while leaving the salt-bloom generic, an improvisation another run may not repeat. Give the thing that burns a countable phrase so the pointer has a real antecedent: "Whenever a Keeper mixes salt-bloom into a batch of mire-essence, that batch of mire-essence burns slowly."

good. one rule covers both quantifications — every arrival of a cold-threshold night, and every unprepared lantern on the Cliff Path — with the dying tied to the night that triggered it and the Cliff Path recorded as a named place the lanterns sit on.
Autumn storms come over the Cold Sea.
Early-winter storms come over the Cold Sea.

good. parses as a fireable generic rule: autumn storms are typed as a kind of storm, the Cold Sea keeps its name plus its 'sea' typing, and 'over the Cold Sea' rides the coming event, so nothing in the sentence is lost.
good. same shape as the first sentence and adjudicated clean — the reviewer's objection to how 'over' was slotted was overruled, so no rewrite is warranted.
The smell of mire-essence is faintly metallic.
good. the smell is its own referent tied to mire-essence, 'metallic' is asserted of it, and 'faintly' is recorded as the degree rather than dropped.
good. parses as a single kind-level colour claim on mire-essence, with the hyphenated colour kept whole as one property.

good. the definite plural becomes a group of copper cauldrons producing mire-essence, with a per-cauldron rule alongside the group event, so both 'do the cauldrons produce it?' and 'does this cauldron produce it?' resolve.
When a tide-pool stone is submerged, salt-bloom grows on that stone.
Salt-bloom crusts have a faint smell of salt.
The salt-bloom is kept in waxed paper packets in the Cauldron Hall store.
Whenever a Keeper adds salt-bloom to mire-essence, that mire-essence burns slowly.

(: sbc_have_rule (Implication (Member $x salt_bloom_crust) (And (Member (sk_have $x) have) (Holder (sk_have $x) $x) (Theme (sk_have $x) (sk_smell $x)) (Member (sk_smell $x) smell) (Member (sk_smell $x) faint) (Of (sk_smell $x) salt))) (STV 0.9 0.9))
